question: Explain what Tailscale Serve does.
raw_answer: Tailscale Serve allows you to route traffic from devices on your Tailscale network (Tailnet) to local services running on a device within that network [1]. It enables private access to these services, ensuring that only authenticated devices within the Tailnet can connect [1]. This functionality is intended for sharing local servers securely within the private network, as opposed to making them accessible on the public internet [3].

passages.heading: Overview
passages.text:
Tailscale provides two complementary features for exposing services:
**Serve**and

**Funnel**. Understanding the difference is crucial for properly securing your self-hosted applications.

passages.heading: Turn one thing off, or reset everything
passages.text:
The `off` form repeats the flags that created the handler. The target is optional:

```
sudo tailscale serve --https=443 --set-path=/api off
sudo tailscale serve --https=8443 off
sudo tailscale serve --tcp=5432 off
```
Name the wrong port or path and you remove nothing, or the wrong thing, which is why `status` comes first. To clear every handler on the node at once:

`sudo tailscale serve reset`
`reset` prints nothing. Run `status` afterwards and it reports `No serve config`. Reset replaces the whole serve config with an empty one, and Funnel listeners live in that same config, so they are cleared too. Re-add any public listener afterwards.

passages.heading: How do I remove a single serve handler without clearing the rest?
passages.text: Repeat the flags that created it and append `off`, for example `sudo tailscale serve --https=443 --set-path=/api off`. Run `sudo tailscale serve status` first to see the exact port and path. `sudo tailscale serve reset` clears every handler on the node instead, including Funnel.
